# Action Interfaces, Skills & Tool Protocols

> How robot capabilities are exposed to models: skills as tools, code-as-action APIs, MCP servers, semantic action spaces, keypoint and affordance constraints.  
> Layer: L2 · 44 entries · [overview](../README.md#interface) · [survey](../SURVEY.md)

**Legend:** 🟢 open · 🟡 partial · 🔵 api · ⚪ closed. Hover a name for the full paper title. Newest first within each year.

**2026**

- ⚪ [**MCP Navigation Representation Layer**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27340 "Spatial and Semantic Reasoning for LLM-Driven Robot Navigation via MCP") · 2026-09 — Non-invasive layer that turns ROS navigation data into LLM-usable context exposed as MCP tools: occupancy grids become metric, pose-aware map images for goal reasoning, and waypoint-level semantic annotations record observations with robot poses. _Note: First-party simulation results (over 97% map coverage; spatial and semantic goal selection)._
- 🟢 [**Isaac ROS 5.0 agent skills**](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/isaac-ros-5-0-agentic-open-source-robotics/) · 2026-09 · NVIDIA — Isaac ROS 5.0 adds skills in the open Agent Skills format so coding assistants can run Isaac ROS workflows, e.g. Mission Control skills that bring up the fleet stack, change maps or fleets and submit and verify missions; more Isaac skills sit in NVIDIA's skills catalog. _Note: Developer-facing: the skills target coding assistants that build and operate Isaac ROS systems rather than a runtime robot action space. The docs also cover Mission Control and Mission Dispatch MCP servers, and the blog announces a standalone agent-ready pick-and-place skill._ [code](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills) · [docs](https://nvidia-isaac-ros.github.io/v/release-5.0/releases/index.html)
- ⚪ [**APPL**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35690 "Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning") · 2026-09 — Uses each skill policy's structural prior (what a behaviour depends on, such as gripper pose relative to an object) both to shape training and, stated in language, as the interface a composing agent reads to decide where the skill applies; a construction agent segments demonstrations into skills.
- 🟢 [**RobotStudio MCP (RAPID program generation)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21417 "Retrieval-grounded robot program generation and simulation-based correction via Model Context Protocol") · 2026-08 — Generates ABB RAPID programs from language with dual-stream RAG over documentation and production templates, and uses an MCP server into ABB RobotStudio to upload code, run simulations and return diagnostics for iterative correction of a pick-and-place cell. _Note: Accepted at CIE53 (2026). The repository ("RobotStudio Agent Bridge") exposes RobotStudio to agents through a Skill-guided CLI or an MCP server._ [code](https://github.com/zhou-zhichao/robotstudio-mcp)
- ⚪ [**Pointing-VLA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23138 "Pointing-VLA: Typed Spatial Grounding Interfaces for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation") · 2026-08 — Replaces text-serialized coordinates with typed hidden-state readout heads (points, object-functional grounding heatmaps, visual trajectories) on Embodied-R1 plus an explicit PICK/PLACE execution contract; also used as spatial guidance for a pi0.5 policy. _Note: First-party results on Bridge/WidowX and a physical pick-and-place setup._
- ⚪ [**Model Hardware Standard (MHS)**](https://www.modelhardwarestandard.com/) · 2026-08 · Anthropic — Driver standard that wraps lab, robotics and manufacturing hardware as discoverable devices with simple read/write operations plus natural-language metadata on states, procedures and limits, reachable via MCP, CLI or code and guarded by deterministic device-level safeguards. _Note: Research preview shared with partners (e.g. Genentech, CMU, HHMI Janelia; vendor support announced by Universal Robots, Doosan Robotics, AWS Strands Robots and Hugging Face LeRobot); Anthropic states it plans to open-source the standard._ [blog](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-hardware-standard-research-preview)
- 🟢 [**open-robot-skills (MORSL)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05369) · 2026-07 · UC Berkeley; NVIDIA — Modular Open Robot Skill Library used by the GaP coding harness: manipulation skills and model-backed tool bundles packaged in the Anthropic Agent Skills (SKILL.md) format, each with scripts and declared exit conditions that generated robot graphs route on. _Note: Described in the GaP paper (see the GaP entry under other); listed separately as the reusable skill artifact._ [code](https://github.com/graph-robots/open-robot-skills) · [project](https://graph-robots.github.io/gap)
- ⚪ [**Contract-Grounded BT Synthesis**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12220 "Contract-Grounded Behavior Tree Synthesis via Coding Agents") · 2026-07 — A coding agent queries a robot-side MCP server for an explicit contract (skill library, permitted behavior-tree operators, optional templates) before synthesizing a behavior tree, which a runtime validation gate checks before execution. _Note: Evaluated on 110 PyRoboSim tasks and 14 tasks on a Husarion Panther (first-party)._ [project](https://jsalfity.github.io/agentic-bt-gen-webviewer/)
- 🟢 [**Agent-Client Protocol for HRI**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14919 "Human-Robot Interaction in GenAI Architectures via the Agent-Client Protocol") · 2026-07 · University of Malaga (MAPIRlab) — Uses the Agent-Client Protocol (from coding agents) for the human-to-agent link and MCP for the agent-to-robot link, giving a three-layer architecture with real-time observability, explicit human authorization and task interruption; tested on a mobile robot with three UIs. _Note: Robot-side ROS 2 code for the Sancho platform is in github.com/MAPIRlab/sancho_robot._ [code](https://github.com/MAPIRlab/sancho-acp-clients)
- ⚪ [**RECENT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07999 "Efficient Skill Grounding via Code Refactoring with Small Language Models") · 2026-06 — Represents skills as executable code and re-grounds them to new embodiments or environments by locally refactoring only their execution bindings with a small language model, rather than regenerating the program; reported to match LLM-based code-as-policies. _Note: ICML 2026; first-party results._
- ⚪ [**Lab Agent Protocol (LAP)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03755 "LAP: An Agent-to-Instrument Protocol for Autonomous Science") · 2026-06 — Protocol design for the agent-to-instrument edge: extends A2A-style discovery and task lifecycles with signed InstrumentCards (capabilities, physical limits), exclusive reservation, safety-fence confirmation tokens for hazardous steps and physically typed measurement results. _Note: Targets self-driving labs; designed to be transport-compatible with A2A/MCP and to wrap device standards such as SiLA 2 and OPC-UA. Specification only; no reference implementation found._
- ⚪ [**VLAs-as-Tools (TAPT)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13119 "Towards Long-horizon Embodied Agents with Tool-Aligned Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2026-05 — A VLM agent plans and recovers while a family of specialized VLA tools executes bounded subtasks through an interface with explicit tool selection and in-execution progress feedback; Tool-Aligned Post-Training makes the VLA tools follow agent invocations. _Note: First-party gains reported on LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin with pi0.5; code announced but not yet released._
- 🟢 [**Octopus Protocol**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09055 "Octopus Protocol: One-Shot Hardware Discovery and Control for AI Agents via Infrastructure-as-Prompts") · 2026-05 — Hardware onboarding in which a coding agent follows markdown specs to enumerate attached devices, infer their capabilities, generate typed MCP tools plus the driver code behind them, deploy the endpoint and keep repairing it; demonstrated with an SO-ARM101 arm and camera. _Note: The authors also report a failure mode of unattended repair loops over 11 hours of operation._ [code](https://github.com/qsimeon/octopus-hw) · [project](https://qsimeon.github.io/octopus-hw/)
- ⚪ [**Embodied Tool Protocol (ETP) / EmbodiedToolBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26637 "Enabling Extensible Embodied Capabilities with Tools") · 2026-05 — Externalizes perception, cognition, reasoning and execution capabilities into 100+ tools under a protocol for registration, discovery, invocation and execution, and benchmarks when, which and how models call them; gains are large for perception and cognition, small for execution. _Note: The code URL given in the paper (github.com/Zxy-MLlab/EmbodiedTool) returned 404 when checked in Sep 2026._ [project](https://racingemperor.github.io/manip-tool-hub/)
- 🟢 [**ROSClaw (OpenClaw-ROS 2)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26997 "ROSClaw: An OpenClaw ROS 2 Framework for Agentic Robot Control and Interaction") · 2026-03 · Kent State University, PlaiPin — Model-agnostic executive layer connecting the OpenClaw agent runtime to ROS 2: dynamic capability discovery, observation normalization, pre-execution action validation in a configurable safety envelope, and audit logging; deployed on wheeled, quadruped and humanoid robots. _Note: Date is the repo's first commit (2026-02); paper posted 2026-03. Repo (messaging-app control via rosbridge) says it is being re-architected; the paper states a full de-anonymized release upon acceptance._ [code](https://github.com/PlaiPin/rosclaw)
- 🟢 [**AgenticROS**](https://agenticros.com/) · 2026-03 · AgenticROS (sponsored by RealSense) — Agent-agnostic interface layer for ROS 2 robots with an OpenClaw/NemoClaw plugin, an MCP server for Claude Code, Codex and Hermes, and Gemini function calling; robots advertise typed capability verbs (drive_base, find_object, ...) extended by skill packages. _Note: Highlighted in NVIDIA's Isaac ROS 5.0 announcement (Sep 2026) as connecting Isaac ROS with Nemotron models and NemoClaw blueprints._ [code](https://github.com/agenticros/agenticros) · [blog](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/isaac-ros-5-0-agentic-open-source-robotics/)
- 🟢 [**DroneServer**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15486 "An LLM-Agnostic, MAVLink-Based Drone Command and Control Interface and Agentic Harness Using the Model Context Protocol") · 2026-01 — MCP server exposing 98 MAVLink/MAVSDK tools (commands, telemetry, missions) for ArduPilot and PX4 to any MCP-capable LLM, treating the model as an untrusted commander with server-side criticality tiers, confirmation handshakes, geofence and audit log. _Note: First-party evaluation over 1,000+ simulated flights (11 models) and three real quadcopters._ [code](https://github.com/PeterJBurke/droneserver)

**2025**

- 🟢 [**RoboNeuron**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10394 "RoboNeuron: A Middle-Layer Infrastructure for Agent-Driven Orchestration in Embodied AI") · 2025-12 — Middleware between MCP-speaking LLM agents and ROS 2 that derives agent-callable tools directly from ROS message schemas, routes semantic tasks to swappable VLA backends and sends basic commands straight to ROS modules. [code](https://github.com/guanweifan/RoboNeuron)
- ⚪ [**Embodied Context Protocol (ECP)**](https://doi.org/10.34133/research.1047 "Orchestrating Embodied Systems through the Embodied Context Protocol: Motivation, Progress, and Directions") · 2025-12 · Shenyang Institute of Automation (CAS); Peking University — Perspective proposing a layered interface protocol (semantic, interaction, adapter and workflow layers) that specifies how embodied task context is represented, how modules report progress and failures, and how heterogeneous backends are composed into workflows. _Note: Published in the journal Research (Dec 2025); no public specification or code found._
- 🟢 [**SkillWrapper**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18203 "SkillWrapper: Generative Predicate Invention for Task-level Robot Planning") · 2025-11 · Brown University — Uses foundation models to actively execute black-box robot skills, invent symbolic predicates from before/after RGB images and build PDDL-style operators with soundness and completeness conditions, so a planner can compose the skills for unseen long-horizon tasks. [code](https://github.com/YzyLmc/skill_wrapper) · [project](https://yzylmc.github.io/skill-wrapper/)
- ⚪ [**SEAM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19315 "Rethinking Intermediate Representation for VLM-based Robot Manipulation") · 2025-11 · CUHK — Semantic Assembly representation that splits the VLM-to-action interface into a concise vocabulary of semantically rich operations and a VLM-friendly grammar, balancing VLM comprehensibility and action generalizability; adds retrieval-augmented part segmentation. _Note: CVPR 2026; first-party real-robot results._
- 🟢 [**ROSBag MCP Server**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03497 "ROSBag MCP Server: Analyzing Robot Data with LLMs for Agentic Embodied AI Applications") · 2025-11 — MCP server that lets LLMs and VLMs query, filter and analyse ROS/ROS 2 bags (trajectories, laser scans, TF, time series) through robotics-specific tools, with a UI used to benchmark tool calling across eight proprietary and open models. _Note: First-party finding that tool-description schema, argument count and number of available tools all affect tool-calling success._ [code](https://github.com/binabik-ai/mcp-rosbags)
- 🟢 [**ROS MCP Server**](https://robotmcp.ai/blog/ros-mcp-server-release) · 2025-09 · RobotMCP — MCP server connecting LLM clients (Claude, GPT, Gemini and others) to ROS 1 and ROS 2 robots through rosbridge, exposing topics, services, actions and parameters with type discovery, without changes to robot code. _Note: Open-source release announced on ROS Discourse in Sep 2025 (PyPI package ros-mcp); earlier versions were public as lpigeon/ros-mcp-server, which now redirects here._ [code](https://github.com/robotmcp/ros-mcp-server)
- ⚪ [**LYRA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18597 "Growing with Your Embodied Agent: A Human-in-the-Loop Lifelong Code Generation Framework for Long-Horizon Manipulation Skills") · 2025-09 · Technical University of Munich — Human-in-the-loop lifelong code generation that encodes human corrections into reusable code skills kept in external memory and retrieved with RAG plus user hints; reports solving very long-horizon tasks such as "build a house" (20+ primitives). _Note: First-party results on Ravens, Franka Kitchen, MetaWorld and real-world settings._
- ⚪ [**Robot Context Protocol (RCP)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11650 "Robot Context Protocol (RCP): A Runtime-Agnostic Interface for Agent-Aware Robot Control") · 2025-06 — Middleware-agnostic protocol over HTTP/WebSocket with schema-driven read, write, execute and subscribe operations, runtime introspection, asynchronous feedback and namespace isolation, letting web clients or LLM agents drive robots, simulators or cloud backends via adapters.
- 🟢 [**KUDA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10546 "KUDA: Keypoints to Unify Dynamics Learning and Visual Prompting for Open-Vocabulary Robotic Manipulation") · 2025-03 · Tsinghua University; UIUC; Columbia University — Keypoint-based target specification that a VLM fills in from language and a keypoint-annotated image, converted into cost functions optimized with a learned neural dynamics model, extending VLM-driven manipulation to deformable and granular objects. _Note: ICRA 2025._ [code](https://github.com/StoreBlank/KUDA) · [project](https://kuda-dynamics.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**IKER**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08643 "A Real-to-Sim-to-Real Approach to Robotic Manipulation with VLM-Generated Iterative Keypoint Rewards") · 2025-02 · UIUC; Stanford University; Amazon; Columbia University — A VLM writes Python reward functions over scene keypoints (Iterative Keypoint Rewards) as a refinable task specification; the rewards train RL policies in a simulated reconstruction of the real scene, which are then deployed back on the real robot. _Note: ICRA 2025._ [code](https://github.com/shivanshpatel35/IKER) · [project](https://iker-robot.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**OmniManip**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03841 "OmniManip: Towards General Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric Interaction Primitives as Spatial Constraints") · 2025-01 · Peking University; AgiBot — Defines interaction primitives (points and directions) in an object's canonical, affordance-based frame so a VLM can express actions as 3D spatial constraints; a dual closed loop resamples primitives with VLM checking and tracks 6D object pose during execution. _Note: CVPR 2025 Highlight; project page lists code as coming soon._ [project](https://omnimanip.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**GeoManip**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09783 "GeoManip: Geometric Constraints as General Interfaces for Robot Manipulation") · 2025-01 · CUHK — Training-free system in which foundation models emit stage-wise geometric constraints between object parts (e.g. knife blade perpendicular to a carrot) in symbolic form, a parser grounds the parts, and a solver optimizes trajectories that satisfy them. _Note: The linked repository currently states the code is under refactoring and not usable._ [project](https://geoconstraintmanip.github.io/)

**2024**

- 🟢 [**ReKep**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01652 "ReKep: Spatio-Temporal Reasoning of Relational Keypoint Constraints for Robotic Manipulation") · 2024-09 · Stanford University; Columbia University — Represents manipulation tasks as VLM-generated Python functions mapping 3D keypoints to costs (relational keypoint constraints); a hierarchical optimizer solves them for SE(3) end-effector poses in a real-time perception-action loop. [code](https://github.com/huangwl18/ReKep) · [project](https://rekep-robot.github.io/)
- 🟡 [**KALIE**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14066 "KALIE: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Models for Open-World Manipulation without Robot Data") · 2024-09 · UC Berkeley; Cornell University — Fine-tunes a VLM to predict point-based affordance representations rather than motor commands, using an affordance-aware synthetic-data pipeline seeded with about 50 human-labelled examples instead of robot data. _Note: Code and human-annotated data are released; fine-tuned weights were not found._ [code](https://github.com/gractang/kalie) · [project](https://kalie-vlm.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sr2022/KALIE_Original_Images)
- ⚪ [**LRLL**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18746 "Lifelong Robot Library Learning: Bootstrapping Composable and Generalizable Skills for Embodied Control with Language Models") · 2024-06 · University of Groningen — Lifelong LLM agent that grows a code skill library over vision and control primitives instead of using a fixed one: soft memory of experiences, self-proposed tasks in simulation, and a skill abstractor that distils experience into new reusable library functions. _Note: ICRA 2024._ [project](https://gtziafas.github.io/LRLL_project/)
- 🟢 [**Agentic Skill Discovery**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15019) · 2024-05 · University of Hamburg — LLM-driven skill discovery from zero skills: the LLM proposes tasks from the scene and robot description and writes reward and success functions for RL training of each skill, and a VLM verifies behaviours before they join the growing skill library. [code](https://github.com/xf-zhao/Agentic-Skill-Discovery) · [project](https://agentic-skill-discovery.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**MOKA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03174 "MOKA: Open-World Robotic Manipulation through Mark-Based Visual Prompting") · 2024-03 · UC Berkeley — Uses a compact point-based affordance representation as the bridge between a VLM and robot motion, eliciting it zero- or few-shot by annotating marks (candidate points, grids) on images and posing affordance reasoning as visual question answering. _Note: RSS 2024._ [code](https://github.com/moka-manipulation/moka) · [project](https://moka-manipulation.github.io/)
- 🟡 [**KAT (Keypoint Action Tokens)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19578 "Keypoint Action Tokens Enable In-Context Imitation Learning in Robotics") · 2024-03 · Imperial College London — Encodes visual observations as keypoint tokens and action trajectories as token sequences so an off-the-shelf text LLM (GPT-4 Turbo) performs few-shot in-context imitation, mapping keypoints to action trajectories without additional training. _Note: RSS 2024. A Colab notebook is linked from the project page. The primary contribution is in-context imitation learning, so it could also be filed under policy._ [project](https://www.robot-learning.uk/keypoint-action-tokens)
- 🟢 [**CoPa**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08248 "CoPa: General Robotic Manipulation through Spatial Constraints of Parts with Foundation Models") · 2024-03 · Tsinghua University; Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute — VLMs ground task-relevant object parts for task-oriented grasping, then emit spatial geometry constraints on those parts from which post-grasp 6-DoF end-effector poses are solved; training-free and composable with high-level planners. [code](https://github.com/HaoxuHuang/copa) · [project](https://copa-2024.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**RoboScript**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14623 "RoboScript: Code Generation for Free-Form Manipulation Tasks across Real and Simulation") · 2024-02 · Shanghai AI Laboratory; HKU — Platform pairing a deployable code-generation manipulation pipeline, built on a unified ROS-based interface to Gazebo and real arms (Franka, UR5), with a benchmark of free-form tasks that probes physical-space and constraint reasoning in LLM-generated code. _Note: No official code link found in the paper or via search (checked Sep 2026)._
- 🟡 [**RoboCodeX**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16117 "RoboCodeX: Multimodal Code Generation for Robotic Behavior Synthesis") · 2024-02 · HKU; Shanghai AI Laboratory — Tree-structured multimodal code generation that decomposes instructions into object-centric manipulation units carrying affordance and safety constraints, then emits robot code; the model is fine-tuned on a collected multimodal reasoning dataset and runs on a ROS/Gazebo stack. _Note: The released repository is the ROS/Gazebo code-generation pipeline; availability of the fine-tuned model weights was not confirmed._ [code](https://github.com/RoboCodeX-source/RoboCodeX_code) · [project](https://sites.google.com/view/robocodexplus)
- ⚪ [**PIVOT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07872 "PIVOT: Iterative Visual Prompting Elicits Actionable Knowledge for VLMs") · 2024-02 · Google DeepMind — Zero-shot pointing interface: candidate actions or waypoints are drawn as labelled marks on the image, the VLM selects the best ones and the proposal distribution is iteratively refined; shown on real navigation and manipulation without robot training data. _Note: A Hugging Face demo Space (pivot-prompt/pivot-prompt-demo) is available._ [project](https://pivot-prompt.github.io/)

**2023**

- 🟢 [**ManipLLM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.16217 "ManipLLM: Embodied Multimodal Large Language Model for Object-Centric Robotic Manipulation") · 2023-12 · Peking University — Adapter-tunes a multimodal LLM to output an object-centric action interface, a contact point and gripper direction reasoned by chain of thought, which an active impedance-adaptation policy then executes in closed loop. [code](https://github.com/clorislili/ManipLLM) · [project](https://sites.google.com/view/manipllm)
- 🟢 [**CodeBotler / RoboEval**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.11183 "Deploying and Evaluating LLMs to Program Service Mobile Robots") · 2023-11 · UT Austin; Northeastern University — CodeBotler generates service-robot programs from language against a robot-agnostic Python embedded DSL of navigation, perception and human-interaction skills; RoboEval checks the programs by executing them and testing traces against temporal-logic specifications. [code](https://github.com/ut-amrl/codebotler) · [project](https://amrl.cs.utexas.edu/codebotler/)
- 🟢 [**BOSS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10021 "Bootstrap Your Own Skills: Learning to Solve New Tasks with Large Language Model Guidance") · 2023-10 · University of Southern California; KAIST — Grows a learned skill library from primitive skills by LLM-guided skill bootstrapping: the LLM proposes meaningful skill chains to practise without task rewards, and the resulting long-horizon behaviours are added to the library for unseen tasks. _Note: CoRL 2023 oral. Skills are learned policies rather than code, so it could also be filed under policy._ [code](https://github.com/clvrai/boss) · [project](https://clvrai.github.io/boss/)
- ⚪ [**SayTap**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.07580 "SayTap: Language to Quadrupedal Locomotion") · 2023-06 · Google DeepMind; University of Tokyo — Uses foot-contact patterns as the interface between an LLM and a learned quadruped locomotion controller: the LLM turns language into contact-pattern templates that an RL policy executes, transferred to real hardware. [project](https://saytap.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**Language to Rewards (L2R)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08647 "Language to Rewards for Robotic Skill Synthesis") · 2023-06 · Google DeepMind — Has an LLM specify reward parameters instead of calling hand-built primitives; a real-time optimizer (MuJoCo MPC) turns them into motion, making reward the interface between language and low-level control for a simulated quadruped, a dexterous hand and a real arm. [code](https://github.com/google-deepmind/language_to_reward_2023) · [project](https://language-to-reward.github.io/)
